questions.question: What is Received Pronunciation (RP)?
options: A prestige accent associated with the upper class, historically used by the BBC
questions.explanation: RP, "the Queen's English", is associated with private schools and the upper class — only about 3% speak "pure" RP.

questions.question: Which accent belongs to which city?
questions.explanation: Scouse is the Liverpool accent, Geordie is Newcastle, Cockney is London's East End and Brummie is Birmingham.

questions.question: What does research show about accent prejudice in Britain?
options: RP speakers are perceived as more competent, while regional accents are seen as friendlier but less professional
All accents are judged exactly the same
Regional accents are seen as more intelligent
Accent has no social meaning in Britain
questions.explanation: Accent discrimination is documented: RP is linked to perceived competence, regional accents to friendliness but lower status.

questions.question: Which regional identities make up the United Kingdom?
options: English, Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish
questions.explanation: The UK contains distinct English, Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish identities.

questions.question: What is "Estuary English"?
options: A widespread accent between RP and Cockney
The accent of the Scottish Highlands
questions.explanation: Estuary English, between RP and Cockney, has become increasingly common as accent attitudes change.
